title: 5 days in Japan: Tokyo, Kyoto

brief.request: Plan a 5-day trip to Japan. Tokyo + Kyoto. $3,000 budget. Love food and temples, hate crowds.

slots.name: Tsukiji Fish Market
slots.why: Breakfast-style seafood market, direct hit on "food"
slots.crowd_tactic: Arrive 07:00 for breakfast, before tour groups land mid-morning

slots.name: Senso-ji
slots.why: Tokyo's most iconic Buddhist temple, the anchor "temples" pick
slots.crowd_tactic: Arrive 06:30, before tour buses and the Nakamise-dori stalls open

slots.name: Omoide Yokocho
slots.crowd_tactic: Arrive before 18:00, before the after-work crowd fills the lanes

slots.name: Nezu Shrine
slots.why: Quiet garden shrine, low-crowd temples option
slots.crowd_tactic: Visit a weekday afternoon, avoid the April azalea festival dates

slots.name: Meiji Jingu
slots.why: Forested Shinto shrine, quiet counterpoint to Senso-ji for temples
slots.crowd_tactic: Arrive weekday 07:00, gates open at dawn, before group tours

slots.name: Yakitori Alley, Yurakucho
slots.why: Under-the-tracks yakitori stalls, lesser-known food find
slots.crowd_tactic: Arrive 17:30 at opening, before the after-work rush

slots.name: Shinkansen, Tokyo to Kyoto (Nozomi), plus station and transfer buffer
slots.why: Direct connection to the Kyoto base for the rest of the trip: 135 min Nozomi ride (seed) + 60 min station/transfer buffer (estimate, not tool-sourced) = 195 min total

slots.name: chao chao gyoza kyoto
slots.why: Highly rated, lesser-known dumpling spot, in Nakagyo Ward
slots.crowd_tactic: Go for lunch before 12:00, before the dinner queue forms

slots.name: Kyoto Shinkyogoku Shopping Street
slots.why: Street snacks and matcha sweets in central Kyoto
slots.crowd_tactic: Avoid weekend afternoons when it is busiest

slots.name: Kiyomizu-dera
slots.why: Landmark wooden temple overlooking the city
slots.crowd_tactic: Arrive 07:30 at opening, before tour groups

slots.name: Nishiki Market
slots.why: "Kyoto's Kitchen" food street, direct hit on "food"
slots.crowd_tactic: Go on a weekday morning at opening, before lunch crowds

slots.name: Kodaiji Temple
slots.why: Temple near Kiyomizu, less crowded alternative, evening light-up hours
slots.crowd_tactic: Visit during late-afternoon light-up hours, thinner crowds than Kiyomizu

slots.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
slots.why: The iconic thousand-torii shrine, the anchor "temples" pick, close to Kyoto Station
slots.crowd_tactic: Arrive 06:00, before tour buses, or hike past the second rest house where crowds thin

slots.name: Free: return to Shimogyo Ward, pack, and head to the station for departure
slots.why: Departure day, buffer before the flight home

stays.why: Senso-ji and the Nakamise food street on the doorstep, and the neighbourhood is quieter at night than Shibuya or Shinjuku, fitting the avoid-crowds note
Central rail hub for day-trip temples, and Kyoto Station's food halls cover the food interest

lines.basis: 4 nights x midpoint $95 (band $70-120 from 03-budget.md, hotel price level unavailable from tool)
Shinkansen fare from 02-logistics.md (seed) $88.48 + 5 days x local transit midpoint $9 (band $6-12) = $45.00
6 temple entries scheduled (Senso-ji, Nezu Shrine, Meiji Jingu, Kiyomizu-dera, Kodaiji Temple, Fushimi Inari Taisha) x midpoint $5.00 (band $3-7)

alternatives: Add a half-day trip to a quieter temple town near Kyoto (Ohara or Arashiyama early morning to dodge crowds), costs about $40 to $70.
Upgrade one or two dinners to a kaiseki or omakase experience, matches the food preference, costs about $60 to $100.
Book a small-group or private early-access temple visit to avoid crowds, costs about $40 to $70.

crowd_strategy: Early-morning temple visits: Fushimi Inari Taisha at 06:00 and Kiyomizu-dera at 07:30, both timed before the tour buses arrive.
Off-peak food picks: Tsukiji Fish Market at its 07:00 opening and Yakitori Alley, Yurakucho at its 17:30 opening, both timed to dodge the tour-group and after-work rush windows.
Lesser-known alternatives over the busiest icons: Nezu Shrine instead of Tokyo's most-visited shrines, and Kodaiji's evening light-up hours instead of daytime Kiyomizu-dera crowds.
Reserved Nozomi Shinkansen seats booked ahead for the Tokyo to Kyoto leg, instead of relying on unreserved cars.

checks.label: Fits in 5 days
checks.reason: Exactly five day headings, numbered Day 1 to Day 5, no gaps and no repeats. Days 1 to 4 carry 3 slots each, day 5 carries 2 (Fushimi Inari plus the departure block), so no day is empty.

checks.label: Includes Tokyo, Kyoto
checks.reason: Tokyo gets full days 1 and 2 with 2 nights in Nishiasakusa. Kyoto gets full days 4 and 5 with 2 nights in Shimogyo. Day 3 is the transfer day and still lands two Kyoto slots.

checks.label: Within $3000
checks.reason: Recomputed from the budget lines: stay 380.00 + transport 133.48 + food 212.50 + activities 30.00 = 755.98 subtotal, buffer 10% = 75.60, total $831.58 against the $3,000 limit, 27.7% of budget. The stated total matches the recomputation to the cent.

checks.label: Matches food, temples
checks.reason: All 5 days carry at least one food or temple slot. Day 1 Tsukiji (food) and Senso-ji (temple), day 2 Nezu Shrine and Meiji Jingu (temple) plus Yakitori Alley (food), day 3 chao chao gyoza and Shinkyogoku (food), day 4 Kiyomizu-dera and Kodaiji (temple) plus Nishiki Market (food), day 5 Fushimi Inari Taisha (temple). 6 temple slots and 6 food slots across the trip.

checks.label: Avoids crowds
checks.reason: All 12 venue slots carry a tactic with a specific time or place, not a generic line. Examples: Fushimi Inari at 06:00 or hike past the second rest house, Kiyomizu-dera at 07:30 opening, Nezu Shrine on a weekday afternoon outside the April azalea dates, Yakitori Alley at 17:30 opening. The two 'n/a, not a venue' entries sit on the Shinkansen leg and the day 5 packing block. Warning, not a fail: the Shinkansen leg does have a real tactic (reserved Nozomi seats, crowd section item 4) that was not carried into the slot row.

checks.label: Travel time realistic
checks.reason: Day 3 allots 195 min for the inter-city move, which is the 135 min Nozomi duration from the logistics table plus a 60 min station buffer, exactly the required allowance. The largest intra-city leg anywhere in the plan is 31 min (day 4, Kiyomizu-dera to Nishiki Market), well under the 90 min ceiling. Warning, not a fail: the day 3 afternoon row repeats 195 in the transit column, which restates the same Tokyo to Kyoto leg instead of giving the short Kyoto Station to Nakagyo hop.
